title: Cardinality under singleton symmetric difference
statement:
Let $S$ be a finite subset of $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ and let $i$ be one of these indices. Then the symmetric difference $S \triangle \{i\}$ satisfies
\[
\abs{S} - 1 \le \abs{S \triangle \{i\}},
\]
where $\abs{S} - 1$ denotes truncated subtraction on the natural numbers (so it is $0$ when $S$ is empty).
hypotheses_covered: S is a finite subset of Fin n
i is an element of Fin n
replaced:
For all $S$ and $i$, $\abs{S} - 1 \le \abs{S \triangle \{i\}}$, the subtraction being
truncated subtraction on $\bbn$.
